candidate_screen.candidate: The political payer is not the direct federal awardee.
candidate_screen.reason: Merely restates verified finding #12766 and predicts no new record.

candidate_screen.candidate: Political payers are drawn from the debt-guarantor subsidiary stack.
candidate_screen.reason: All three appear in Exhibit 22, but the table contains roughly 62 guarantor rows. The high base rate makes the overlap non-diagnostic without a peer or nonpayer denominator.

candidate_screen.candidate: The October 2025 switch to Reentry tracks its SAM activation or Trump-II award acceleration.
candidate_screen.reason: The current SAM activation field is not a historical status snapshot, the first Reentry receipt predates the shown activation date, and one temporal coincidence cannot support a mechanism.

candidate_screen.candidate: MUR 7180 alone caused GEO to stop using GCH and rotate later payers.
candidate_screen.reason: Temporal order exists, but no contemporaneous post-MUR approval or causal record is available. MUR awareness is retained as one predicted record under the broader selection-rule hunch.

candidate_screen.candidate: A recurring centralized selection step may compare proposed political payer entities by federal-award/legal status.
candidate_screen.reason: The twice-changing payer across three independent contexts adds a mechanism not captured by finding #12766 and predicts concrete approval, legal-review, account, and future-behavior records.

novelty_assessment.base_rate_control: The guarantor overlap was rejected because approximately 62 entities are listed; no peer-company baseline yet exists for political payer rotation.
novelty_assessment.genuinely_new_mechanism: A repeatable entity-selection rule, not the already-known payer/awardee split.

working_hypothesis_prediction: Common parent-level approvers or counsel appear across payment packets from all three subsidiaries.
Payment-specific review refers to 52 U.S.C. 30119, MUR 7180, SAM, UEIs, contracts, or candidate-entity award status.
Historical or future payer changes continue to select entities with no exact direct-award match when a candidate payer's award status changes.
working_hypothesis_disconfirmation: Payer identity follows longstanding bank-account ownership and ordinary nonpolitical cash activity without award-status review.
A full-cycle denominator shows direct-awardee corporate payers at comparable rates.
Payer transitions align with reorganizations or cash sweeps while award status remains unchanged or irrelevant.
null_prediction: Each payer uses an established account also used for ordinary expenses.
Rotation aligns with segment cash, tax ownership, financing, guarantor, or reorganization changes.
Approval records contain ordinary authority and budget checks but no entity-level contractor-status comparison.
null_disconfirmation: Repeated approval packets explicitly compare candidate payers by direct-award status.
Legal reviewers direct switches after award or MUR changes.
Payment-specific transfers fund otherwise inactive payer accounts and ordinary account explanations fail.

working_hypothesis.title: GEO applies an award-status-aware legal-entity selection step to corporate political payments

null_hypothesis.title: Ordinary cash management and REIT/legal separation explain GEO payer rotation without an award-status criterion

ach_group.least_evidence_against_verdict: Formal tie: neither hypothesis has inconsistent evidence. H0 has the only diagnostic-consistent evidence currently scored, so the working hunch is not preferred. The record is unresolved until the predicted approval/account records or cross-cycle counterexamples are obtained.

hunch_gate.scope: Passed for a testable research hypothesis only; did not pass as an evidentiary conclusion or misconduct theory.
hunch_gate.next_test: Execute lead #61546 and human action #48 with symmetric searches for H1, H0, and counterexamples.
